artboards.title: Browse — one thing, sorted and narrowed
Browse — one entry and what it connects to

annotations.text:
Vocabulary rule (UI-2, BR-6)

Nothing on any of these screens requires knowing what a collection, column, schema, index, query, constraint or nullable is. Those words do not appear.

"things you've stored" · "what a conference keeps" · "some words" · "a day" · "an amount of money" · "always needed" · "no two the same" · "often left empty"

Two surfaces, one switch (D-13)

Chat is where work happens and nothing structural is ever named. Browse is where everything is visible.

Nobody needs Browse to use the application. It is for looking, checking and reassurance — a person who cannot see what a system did with their data does not trust it.

Everything in Browse costs nothing (BR-4, scenario S-8)

Sorting, narrowing, opening an entry and reading what it keeps all go straight to storage as a declarative query. No model is called, so the whole of S-8 records zero tokens.

The footer of the table says so out loud.

The diagram (TR-5, TR-6, D-9)

Drawn natively — a GraphicsView over Microsoft.Maui.Graphics, with the layout computed in plain testable C#.

Participants across the top, lifelines down, one call per row. It grows while the request runs. The selected block opens the panel below it: a data change shows before beside after, a model call shows tokens and timing.

Additive happens, destructive asks (D-7)

Adding City to every conference needed no permission — it is in the Chat artboard as something that simply happened.

Removing notes is a loss, so it is stated as a loss: how many, three real examples, what survives, and that it cannot be undone. Counts and examples, never schema terms (UI-4).

The last line is honest about versioning: getting this back is a later feature (deltas), not one that exists.

Lifted from the existing app, not invented

Open Sans · 7px radii · 13px body, 12/11 secondary · 8px gaps · 12,8 and 14,10 paddings.

#111111 window · #202023 panels · #252529 raised · #303035 hover and lines · #38383D borders · #A79BD8 and #6B5FA8 violet from MAUI's #512BD4 · #E57373 and #C0392B for loss.
